Working from the article text provided directly. Here is my analysis:

---

**Published online:**
September 02, 2026

**Geographic focus:**
Global — with primary focus on US, Middle East (Iran/Jordan/Iraq), Japan, New Zealand, Europe (Germany, UK)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps US-Iran exchange of fire since July, recent bond yield moves
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — BOJ Sept 17-18 meeting, oil shock inflation feed-through, tightening financial conditions
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO] — no explicit multi-quarter/year outlook

**Synopsis:**
US-Iran hostilities have resumed after a pause since July, triggering an oil price surge (Brent above $95) and pushing the US 10-year Treasury yield to a 3-year intraday high of 4.8122%. Bond markets are under compounding pressure: geopolitical risk, fiscal deficit concerns from bond vigilantes, an oil-driven inflation re-acceleration, and hawkish signals from the BOJ (which risks repatriating Japanese capital from global bond markets). Equities sold off broadly across Asia and early European futures. The RBNZ hiked 25bps but signaled dovishness, weakening the NZD. Key near-term events include Broadcom/Snowflake earnings and the BOJ meeting Sept 17-18.

---

**Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?**
Relevance: YES — the article directly references the US 10-year yield hitting a 3-year high (4.8122%), US-Iran geopolitical escalation driving oil/inflation dynamics, and S&P 500 e-mini futures pricing.

**Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 75 (moderately-high — the article is not about Fed rate decisions directly, but rising yields, oil-driven inflation, and bond vigilante pressure all implicitly point to a higher-for-longer or upward rate trajectory)
Probability of increase: 65%

**Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?**
Relevance: 15 (low — there is no mention of the Fed pausing or holding; the narrative is dominated by upward yield pressure)
Probability of holding: 20%

**Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 5 (very low — no dovish Fed signals or rate cut discussion present)
Probability of decrease: 15%

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: 75 (meaningfully hawkish — the combination of a 3-year high on the 10-year yield at 4.8122%, renewed oil shock stoking inflation, bond vigilante pressure on deficit spending, and Japanese repatriation risk removing a key anchor for global bond demand all reinforce a hawkish/tightening bias for US rates with no offsetting dovish signals present in the article)
